tasks.title: Shared harness-owned skill set; init vendors only it
tasks.objective: Define the harness-owned skill set (forge) once in scaffold.py and re-express upgrade's CLAUDE_HARNESS_OWNED on it so the two cannot drift. Route init through it: drop .claude from the wholesale COPY_TREES and copy the .claude harness files plus only .claude/skills/forge; replace the wholesale .codex/skills copytree with only .codex/skills/forge; .codex/agents and config copy as-is, still through the existing boundary helpers. Add the agreement test and an init decoy-skill test.
acceptance_criteria: forge init from a source repo carrying a decoy .claude/skills/decoy/SKILL.md (with a root-level canon target) produces a scaffold that does NOT contain decoy, and check_dual_runtime is clean on the scaffold.
init copies the harness .claude files (CLAUDE.md, settings.json) and only the harness skill dirs .claude/skills/forge and .codex/skills/forge; .codex/agents and .codex config copy as before.

The harness-owned skill set is defined in ONE place; upgrade's CLAUDE_HARNESS_OWNED and init read that same definition (no second hard-coded list), proven by a test. (adopt joins the agreement in FORGE-VENDOR-1.2.)
forge init of symphony-forge produces the same scaffold as before (existing init scaffold tests stay green, unweakened).
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "init or scaffold or vendor or harness_owned or dual_runtime"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That init copies ONLY the harness skill (forge), not the source repo's other .claude/.codex skills — the decoy test must fail if the wholesale copy returns. That the harness-owned skill set is a single source of truth (no second hard-coded 'forge' list that can drift from upgrade). That a normal symphony-forge init is byte-for-byte unchanged (its .claude/.codex IS the manifest).

tasks.title: adopt vendors only the harness-owned skill
tasks.objective: Replace adopt's wholesale .claude and .codex/skills vendoring with manifest-scoped copies: the .claude harness files plus only .claude/skills/forge and .codex/skills/forge, keeping adopt's vendor_file boundary check; .codex/agents and config as before. Also route upgrade's .codex/skills through HARNESS_OWNED_SKILLS (it still iterated the source) so all three share one skill set. Add an adopt decoy-skill test and the three-way agreement test.
acceptance_criteria: forge adopt from a source repo carrying a decoy .claude/skills/decoy/SKILL.md does NOT vendor decoy into the target, and check_dual_runtime is clean on the result.
adopt vendors only the harness .claude files and the harness skill dirs (.claude/skills/forge, .codex/skills/forge), reading the same shared skill set as init and upgrade.
A test asserts init, adopt AND upgrade all read the one shared harness-owned skill set (now that adopt is routed) — no command carries a second hard-coded list.
forge adopt of an existing project behaves as before (existing adopt tests stay green, unweakened).
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "adopt or vendor or harness_owned"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That adopt's wholesale .claude/.codex-skills vendoring is genuinely replaced (not left alongside), that it reads the SAME shared skill set as init (Task 1), and that adopt's per-file boundary check (vendor_file) is preserved. That no existing adopt test was weakened.

tasks.title: Gate the FORGE-INIT-1 fixture tests; client-CI simulation
tasks.objective: Add a presence-keyed skip guard to the three FORGE-INIT-1-bound tests (historical_decomposition_artifacts, precontract_stories_are_marked, shipped_roadmap_satisfies_the_story_contract) so they skip when the fixture (.factory/history/FORGE-INIT-1/) is absent and still run in symphony-forge. Add a client-CI simulation test that scaffolds from a source carrying a client skill and asserts check_dual_runtime is clean.
acceptance_criteria: The three FORGE-INIT-1 fixture-bound tests carry a skip guard keyed on the fixture's presence; they execute in symphony-forge (fixture present) and skip when it is absent.

A test simulates a client-repo run of the vendored checks: it scaffolds from a source carrying a client .claude/skills/<x>/SKILL.md, runs check_dual_runtime on the scaffold, and asserts it is clean (no dangling canon).
The full suite stays green in symphony-forge with no test weakened.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "historical_decomposition or precontract or shipped_roadmap or client_repo or vendored_scaffold or dual_runtime"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the skip guard keys on the FIXTURE's presence (so it is a no-op in symphony-forge and only skips where the fixture is genuinely absent), not on a coarse 'am I the harness' check that could hide a real failure. That the client-CI simulation actually reproduces the reported failure mode (a client skill with a root-level canon target) and would fail if init's filtering regressed.
